items.detail: Add only NONE -> D-4-2 (abroad). D-4-2 is a status people enter from abroad. The live programme is K-Trainee (D-4-2K, company-tailored internship): staff of overseas subsidiaries from 9 countries (exactly the map's asiaPilot group: VN, CN, TH, JP, IN, ID, MY, SG, PH), 6 months plus 1, extendable to 1 year, then a required return home. Other D-4-2 trainees (public institute, company or international organisation) also come in on a CCVI or consular visa. data/visadocs.yaml has only the K-Trainee extension list, with the notice that the manual gives no other D-4-2 list, and it has no D-4-2 change list, so do not add in-Korea edges into D-4-2. Follow-up: D-4-2's own next list (D-2-2, D-2-3, D-10-1, E-7-1, F-2-3) is wrong for K-Trainee interns, who must go home. Give those moves a note, or treat K-Trainee as abroad-only. Suggested note on the NONE edge: 'K-Trainee (D-4-2K) only for citizens of VN, CN, TH, JP, IN, ID, MY, SG, PH employed by a Korean company's overseas subsidiary.'
edges: NONE -> D-4-2 (abroad; K-Trainee D-4-2K limited to asiaPilot nationalities)

items.detail: Add NONE -> E-6-2 (abroad, CCVI route). E-6-2 (performers at tourist hotels and entertainment venues) is still a live sub-status: the manual's E-6 extension list asks for documents marked 'E-6-2자격만 징구' (health-insurance confirmation, letter of guarantee). New E-6-2 holders come in through the E-6 visa issuance confirmation (CCVI) for performances under the Public Performance Act, which needs a performance recommendation from the Korea Media Rating Board (영상물등급위원회). Do not add in-Korea edges into E-6-2. There is no E-6-2 change list, and the E-7 change list explicitly excludes E-6-2 holders, which shows how restrictive the manual is about this status. Suggest a short caution note on the edge: strict screening, and the venue is inspected.
edges: NONE -> E-6-2 (abroad, CCVI with a Korea Media Rating Board (영상물등급위원회) recommendation)

items.detail: E-7-Y (국내성장인력) is obtained only by a change of status inside Korea. Eligibility: age 18–24, 7+ years in Korea before turning 18, and Korean elementary, middle and high school (GED counts; KIIP level 5 can replace a missing stage). The applicant then needs a job. No NONE edge. Add in-Korea edges from the statuses such youths hold in the map: D-4-3 (school student), F-3 (dependent child), F-1 (family visitor), and D-10-1 (the manual's D-10 change list has a 'Foreign youth raised in Korea (age 18-24)' case, so the job-search route leads to E-7-Y). The target's own gating (age [18,24], koreanEdu 1) already filters these. The exact list of prior statuses is not quoted in any primary text I could reach, so it is inferred. Under the child-education programme, children also hold G-1 sub-codes, which the map does not model. For consistency, also add D-4-3, F-3 and F-1 -> D-10-1 with the youth case's needs. The programme runs until 2028-03-31.
edges: D-10-1 -> E-7-Y (in Korea; youth raised in Korea who found a job)

items.detail: No edge into H-2 from anywhere (NONE, C-3-8 or any other status). New H-2 applications stopped on 2026-02-12 and ethnic Koreans now enter on F-4. Existing holders can stay until their maximum period and can switch to F-4 at any time; the change fee is waived until 2027-12-31. Keep H-2 as a current-visa start and keep its outgoing edges (F-4, F-5-14, E-7-4, E-7-4R). The manual still lists H-2 workers in the E-7-4/E-7-4R change lists. MOJ reported 48,905 H-2 -> F-4 change applications and 44,340 approvals between 2026-02-12 and 2026-07-31.

items.detail: F-2-4 is already offered from G-1-5. It looks unreachable only because nothing leads into G-1-5. Keep G-1-5 -> F-2-4 (in Korea). It stands for the outcome of a recognised refugee claim, and the manual's F-2 change list covers it. Add no other edges: recognition is a Ministry of Justice decision, not something a reader applies for from other statuses. Refugees resettled from abroad (난민법 제24조, from memory) arrive already recognised, which is not a route the map can gate. A recognised refugee's spouse and minor children get F-1 (manual 29 › 9), not F-2-4; see F-1. The map should also allow F-2-4 as a reader's current visa (it already exists as a node).

Add the same in-Korea edges the map already has into F-2-8: B-1, B-2, C-3-1, C-3-4 and C-3-9 -> F-2-81. Visadocs has no abroad list for F-2-8 or F-2-81, so there is no NONE edge. Rename it from 'Child of...' to 'Family (spouse or unmarried child) of a tourism/resort investor', because the manual covers the spouse too and adult unmarried children must prove they are unmarried.

items.detail: F-2-13 is the family code of the public-interest investor (F-2-12). It is changed in Korea in the same manual section as F-2-12 (F-2-12, 13, 14), and the investor's spouse and unmarried children apply alongside the investor. items.detail: The Minister of Justice grants F-2-16 at their discretion to a person they recognise for a special contribution to Korea or to the public interest. There is no application route, no document list in visadocs and no eligibility the map can test. The only real precedent is the 2021 Afghan special contributors, who entered on a C-3 arrival visa, changed to F-1 and then got F-2 by ministry decision. Do not add F-1 -> F-2-16 or C-3 -> F-2-16, since readers cannot choose this step. Keep F-2-16 as a current-visa start with its existing next steps (F-5-28, F-5-29).

Add F-3 -> F-2-T1 (in Korea), for the dependants of an E-7-T, E-7-1, E-1 or E-3 holder who moves up to F-2-T. Add F-2-71 -> F-2-T1 (in Korea), for the family of an F-2-7 holder who moves up to F-2-T. items.detail: F-1 has many sub-types. Most are issued from abroad. The manual sections include: F-1-5 (a marriage migrant's parent or family coming to help with childcare or a serious illness), F-1-D (digital nomad), parents of highly skilled people, investors and students, the parent of an F-2-T holder, domestic helpers (F-1-21 to F-1-24), the parent accompanying a school student, parents of F-4 or H-2 holders, and first-generation Joseonjok. So add NONE -> F-1 (abroad). Two in-Korea routes are also documented. F-3 -> F-1: dependants of a principal who changes to F-2-7 but earns less than 1× GNI go to F-1 (manual 29 › 11); this matches the map's existing F-1/F-3 -> F-2-71 'once ≥1× GNI'. C-3-8 -> F-1: the parent of an F-4 holder (manual 36 › 6 › 라 › □ 체류자격 변경). Optional: G-1-5 -> F-1 for the spouse or minor child of a newly recognised refugee (29 › 9). F-1 is broad, so the NONE edge needs a note like 'only for listed family, helper or digital-nomad cases'.
edges: F-3 -> F-1 (in Korea; family of a new F-2-7 earning under 1× GNI)
C-3-8 -> F-1 (in Korea; parent of an F-4 holder)

items.detail: Recommended: do not draw edges into G-1-5. Legally, G-1-5 is reached by filing a refugee application, which only a person already in Korea (any status, including overstay) or at a port of entry can do. Never add NONE -> G-1-5: a claim cannot be filed from abroad. The map cannot test refugee eligibility (persecution), and offering 'apply for refugee status' as a next step from every visa would present asylum as a migration option. Keep G-1-5 as a current-visa start with next steps F-2-4 (recognised) and G-1-6 (humanitarian stay). If the maintainer still wants edges, the correct form is 'any in-Korea status -> G-1-5 (in Korea)', not a selected few. Work permission comes only after 6 months (난민법 제40조, per the extract).

items.detail: Add G-1-5 -> G-1-6 (in Korea). G-1-6 is the humanitarian-stay holder: refugee status refused, but a humanitarian stay granted. Like G-1-5 -> F-2-4, it is the Ministry's decision on the same claim, not a separate application, so the note should say so: 'If refugee status is refused but a humanitarian stay is granted (decided by the Ministry of Justice).' G-1-6 also stays valid as a start. Some practitioner sites give conflicting codes (G-1-6 as 'under appeal', G-1-10 as humanitarian). The manual-derived visadocs case supports G-1-6 = humanitarian stay. It is renewed a year at a time.
edges: G-1-5 -> G-1-6 (in Korea; outcome of a refused refugee claim)

items.detail: Keep NONE -> B-1 as a first status, but it is not a visa. B-1 is the status given at the border to nationals of visa-waiver-agreement countries, so no consulate issues anything. That is why visadocs has no abroad list for it, and none should be added. The countries: visaWaiver gate already limits it correctly. Fix the wording: NONE's 'how' says 'your first visa is issued by a Korean consulate or online', so the B-1 move should say 'No visa: enter visa-free under the agreement; a K-ETA is needed unless your country is exempt', and the docs panel should show K-ETA instead of an abroad list. The manual's B-1 notice says extensions and status changes are in principle refused (exceptions only). Any in-Korea move out of B-1 in the map is therefore an exception to check separately.
edges: NONE -> B-1 (visa-free entry, not a visa issuance; keep)

items.quote: 사증면제(B-1): 대한민국과 사증면제협정을 체결한 국가의 국민으로서 그 협정에 따른 활동을 하려는 사람. visadocs notice: 'Visa-free entrants are in principle not given an extension or a change of status; anyone who needs to stay longer should come back with a visa.'

items.detail: Keep NONE -> B-2 as a first status, relabelled as visa-free entry for tourism or transit, as for B-1. B-2 is granted at entry to nationals of countries Korea admits without a visa by its own rules (the map's visaFree group), and to some transit passengers. No visa is issued, so no abroad list is expected; a K-ETA is needed unless exempt. The manual's B-2 notice likewise says extensions and changes are refused in principle.
edges: NONE -> B-2 (visa-free entry, not a visa issuance; keep)

items.quote: 관광·통과(B-2): 관광․통과 등의 목적으로 대한민국에 사증 없이 입국하려는 사람

items.detail: Keep NONE -> E-7-S1 (abroad). E-7-S1 (high-income professional: income of 3× GNI or more, any job except simple labour or jobs closed to foreigners) is an E-7 sub-status. It is issued through the general E-7 visa-issuance (CCVI) route. The manual has no separate E-7-S issuance or change section, so visadocs maps only the shared E-7 extension list. The fix is to point E-7-S1's abroad documents at E-7-1's abroad list, not to drop the edge. Evidence that people hold it after a visa from abroad: the F-3 visa list waives the sponsor's financial proof when the principal is E-7-S1. Also missing: in-Korea edges. The E-7 change list covers 'Registered D-1, D-2, D-4~D-10, E-1~E-6 (not E-6-2) holders and their F-3 spouses changing to E-7', so E-7-S1 should be offered from the same statuses as E-7-1 (at least D-2-x, D-10-1, E-1–E-6 except E-6-2, and F-3).
edges: NONE -> E-7-S1 (abroad; keep, docs = E-7 CCVI list)
D-2-x, D-10-1, E-1..E-6 (not E-6-2), F-3 -> E-7-S1 (in Korea; same sources as E-7-1)

E-7 change case: 'Registered D-1, D-2, D-4~D-10, E-1~E-6 (not E-6-2) holders and their F-3 spouses changing to E-7'. Manual (R1): 소득이 전년도 1인당 국민총소득의 3배 이상이면서 단순노무, 선량한 풍속에 반하는 업종, 기타 외국인의 취업을 제한하는 직종에 취업하지 않으면

items.detail: Same as E-7-S1. E-7-S2 (high-tech industry professional, 60+ points, outside the listed E-7 occupations) is issued through the general E-7 CCVI route, so keep NONE -> E-7-S2 (abroad) and use E-7-1's abroad document list. Add in-Korea edges from the statuses the E-7 change list covers (D-2-x, D-10-1, E-1–E-6 except E-6-2, F-3). The 2023 introduction of the negative-list E-7-S was reported as open to new hires in high-tech industries. I found no primary text on the E-7-S issuance procedure itself, so confidence is moderate.
edges: NONE -> E-7-S2 (abroad; keep, docs = E-7 CCVI list)
D-2-x, D-10-1, E-1..E-6 (not E-6-2), F-3 -> E-7-S2 (in Korea; same sources as E-7-1)

items.quote: Manual (findings.md): '국내에 1년 이상 네거티브 방식의 전문인력 자격으로 체류하면서 E-7-S1은 소득요건이 유지되고 E-7-S2는 점수요건 60점 이상을 충족하고 사회통합프로그램 3단계 이상 이수'. Extract: 고기술 산업의 신규 채용 인력이나 전년도 한국 국민총소득(GNI)을 넘는 임금을 받는 근로자가 신청할 수 있다고 보도
